facts.text: Early settlement of the Whiting area began in the 1880s, as homesteaders sought fertile bottomlands for agriculture and livestock ranching.
Whiting sits along the eastern foothills of the Laramie Range, where the Rocky Mountains' front range meets the Great Plains.
The Homestead Act of 1862 helped spur small-scale farming ventures in southeastern Wyoming, including areas near present-day Whiting.
Whiting occupies gently rolling plains and terrace remnants formed by deposits along streams draining toward the Laramie and North Platte Rivers.
Whiting experiences a cold semi-arid climate with hot summers and winters where average lows can drop to 14 degrees Fahrenheit.
Annual precipitation in Whiting totals about 15 inches, occurring mostly during spring and summer thunderstorms.
